biological.citation: Ayte et al. 2000 - Promoter-driven splicing regulation in fission yeast (PMID: 18815595)
biological.summary: Rem1 is a meiosis-specific cyclin in Schizosaccharomyces pombe whose expression is regulated by both transcription and splicing. Rem1 deletion causes decreased intragenic meiotic recombination and delayed onset of meiosis I. Ectopic expression in mitotic cells induces G1 arrest and mitotic catastrophes. Splicing regulation depends on forkhead transcription factors Mei4 (positive regulator) and Fkh2 (negative regulator).

biological.citation: Prakash et al. 1989 - Spontaneous mitotic recombination in yeast: the hyper-recombinational rem1 mutations are alleles of the RAD3 gene (PMID: 2840336)
biological.summary: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, rem1 mutations are alleles of RAD3 that confer high levels of spontaneous mitotic gene conversion, crossing over, and mutation. rem1 strains show distinct genetic interactions with recombination-repair pathway mutations compared to UV-sensitive RAD3 alleles. Double mutants of rem1 with recombination-repair defects are inviable, suggesting rem1 functions in a recombination-repair pathway distinct from UV excision repair.

biological.citation: Ayte et al. 2001 - A meiosis-specific cyclin regulated by splicing is required for proper progression through meiosis (PMID: 16024772)
biological.summary: Rem1 is a fission yeast B-type cyclin present exclusively during meiosis. Rem1-deficient cells show impaired meiotic recombination and require Rem1 for premeiotic DNA synthesis when Cig2 is absent. Rem1 splicing is positively regulated by Mei4 and negatively by Cig2, ensuring timely cyclin appearance during meiotic progression.

biological.citation: Omelchenko et al. 2013 - Adrenergic signaling controls RGK-dependent trafficking of cardiac voltage-gated L-type Ca2+ channels through PKD1 (PMID: 22076634)
biological.summary: Rem1, a member of the RGK (Rad-Gem/Kir-related) GTPase family, is strongly and specifically expressed in cardiac tissue. Phosphorylation of Rem1 at Ser18 by protein kinase D1 (downstream of α1-adrenergic signaling) relieves Rem1-mediated inhibition of voltage-gated L-type calcium channels, increasing channel activity and plasma membrane expression in neonatal cardiomyocytes and adult ventricular myocytes.

biological.citation: Liang et al. 2020 - Ras associated with diabetes may play a role in fracture nonunion development in rats (PMID: 31830958)
biological.summary: Rem1, an RGK subfamily member, was analyzed alongside Rad in rat fracture healing models. Real-time PCR showed Rad expression increased significantly in nonunions versus standard healing fractures at post-fracture days 14, 21, and 28. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed similar immunolocalization patterns of Rad and Rem1 in both fracture types at days 14 and 21.

biological.citation: Yamaguchi et al. 2010 - Rapid Oligo-Galacturonide Induced Changes in Protein Phosphorylation in Arabidopsis (PMID: 26811356)
biological.summary: REM1.3, a putative scaffold protein, was identified as a phosphoprotein with rapid OG-induced phosphorylation changes in Arabidopsis. Genetic analysis showed that null mutations in REM1.3 enhance a dominant WAK allele, indicating REM1.3 plays a role in the oligo-galacturonide-induced cell wall stress response pathway.

biological.citation: Cerutti et al. 2011 - REM1, a new type of long terminal repeat retrotransposon in Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (PMID: 16287873)
biological.summary: CrREM1 is a Ty3-gypsy-related LTR retrotransposon identified in the green alga Chlamydomonas reinhardtii. It is present in low copy number, highly methylated, and exhibits inducible transpositional activity. CrREM1 amplifies copy number during foreign DNA integration and genetic crosses but shows restricted integration despite high transcriptional activity, suggesting a regulatory mechanism to minimize genomic damage.

biological.citation: Tanaka et al. 2000 - Negative control contributes to an extensive program of meiotic splicing in fission yeast (PMID: 15893732)
biological.summary: Rem1 is one of two cyclins (along with crs1) identified as meiotically spliced transcripts in Schizosaccharomyces pombe that retain introns during vegetative growth. Splicing regulation occurs via inhibition in mitotic cells rather than positive activation, with regulatory sequences located outside coding regions far from target introns.

biological.citation: Scheffzek et al. 2007 - Biochemical and structural characterization of the gem GTPase (PMID: 17107948)
biological.summary: Rem1 is a member of the RGK protein family (Rad, Gem, Rem1, Rem2) that constitute an atypical branch of the Ras superfamily. RGK proteins exhibit lower GDP/GTP binding affinities (micromolar range) compared to H-Ras, higher GTPase activity regulated by N- and C-terminal extensions, and carry bulky DXWEX motifs in switch II that affect nucleotide binding and regulation.

biological.citation: Tian et al. 2024 - Mining of Root-Specific Expression Genes and Their Core Cis-Regulatory Elements in Plants (PMID: 40004183)
biological.summary: REM1 (Root Expression Motif) represents a newly identified cis-acting regulatory element predicted to determine root tissue-specific expression patterns in plants. REM2, another identified motif, is conserved across Arabidopsis and rice, suggesting these elements are important genetic resources for regulating spatiotemporal gene expression in synthetic circuits.
biological.sample_size: 489 RTEGs in Arabidopsis, 276 in rice, 728 in maize; 34 conserved across three species
